interface.signature: def getHappyString(n: int, k: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: n is a positive integer between 1 and 10 (inclusive), and k is a positive integer between 1 and 100 (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(c in ['a', 'b', 'c'] for c in return_value) and all(return_value[i] != return_value[i + 1] for i in range(len(return_value) - 1)) if return_value != '' else True
postconditions.description: If the return value is non-empty, it is a happy string of length n (all characters are in ['a', 'b', 'c'] and no two adjacent characters are equal).

postconditions.expression: return_value == '' or (len(return_value) == n and k <= sum(3 * 2 ** (i - 1) for i in range(1, n + 1)))
postconditions.description: If the return value is non-empty, it is the k-th lexicographically ordered happy string of length n. If there are fewer than k happy strings of length n, return an empty string.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '' or (len(return_value) == n and all(return_value[i] != return_value[i + 1] for i in range(len(return_value) - 1)))
postconditions.description: The returned string (if non-empty) is a valid happy string of length n, ensuring no two adjacent characters are the same.
